sections.title: باب 2 — متن (10)

paras.text: In the CRC, emphasis has been placed on respecting the self-esteem of children. According to Article 16 of the convention, the protection of the honour and reputation of children shall be ensured. According to Article 37, states are bound to provide protection to children from inhuman, torturous and cruel punishments and behaviour. According to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions), the self-esteem of children should be taken care of. Before Islam the Arabs considered children their personal property (estate). The Quran strictly negated this. In the world convention on children this too has been negated. According to Article 19, for states it is necessary to take suitable legislative, administrative and social and educational measures to save the child from physical and mental violence, injury or their misuse, neglect, bad behaviour and exploitation etc. In the Quran, in nineteen verses, harsh and cruel behaviour with orphan boys and girls has been prohibited. It is the right of children that they be saved from physical and moral harm. In Islam children have been given the right of inheritance.

Respect for self-esteem:

In the CRC, emphasis has been placed on respecting the self-esteem of children. According to Article 16 of the convention, the protection of the honour and reputation of children shall be ensured. According to Article 37, states are bound to provide protection to children from inhuman, torturous and cruel punishments and behaviour. According to the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions), the self-esteem of children should be taken care of. Before Islam the Arabs considered children their personal property (estate). The Quran strictly negated this. In the world convention on children this too has been negated. According to Article 19, for states it is necessary to take suitable legislative, administrative and social and educational measures to save the child from physical and mental violence, injury or their misuse, neglect, bad behaviour and exploitation etc. In the Quran, in nineteen verses, harsh and cruel behaviour with orphan boys and girls has been prohibited. It is the right of children that they be saved from physical and moral harm. In Islam children have been given the right of inheritance.

Foster mother and adoption:

According to Article 20 of the convention the state shall arrange foster mothers for orphan children, make Islamic orphanages (dar-ul-kafala), arrange adoption, taking as one’s own or making mutabanna, or arrange upbringing in suitable institutions. In Islam foster mothers have been encouraged. Among the Arabs the custom of the foster mother existed, i.e. other women used to suckle children.

Protection from drugs:

In the world convention states are bound to save children from the use of drugs and from their trade. In Islam there is a ban on trading in and using drugs for every human being. In this way children too are included in it.

Education:

In the convention great emphasis has been placed on the education of children. Great responsibilities have been placed on the state and parents. Education is the right of children. The saying of the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) is that a father cannot give his child anything better than education. In the battle of Badr, for the freedom of non-Muslim prisoners this condition was set, that whoever taught ten Muslim children would be given freedom. From this the importance of worldly knowledge also becomes clear. In Bukhari’s Book of Knowledge it is that if someone spends the whole night in the mosque offering supererogatory prayers, it is better than that that he teaches the child manners. In Islam there is no gender discrimination for the acquisition of education.

paras.text: According to Article 7 of the convention, states shall ensure the right of children to care and attention from their parents. In Islam stress has been laid on mercy and kindness to children. In Islam children have been given the rights of feeding, giving clothes and protection until they reach maturity. In the Quran, according to Surah Al-Baqarah, “and the one whose child it is, upon him is their food and clothing according to custom.” It is the right of children that they obtain love and affection from parents. Getting equal status is also their right. Above all monetary gifts …

He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) walked towards the tent of Hazrat Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) and asked about the children. Suddenly Hazrat Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) came running out and embraced him (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions). Responsibilities of parents

According to Article 7 of the convention, states shall ensure the right of children to care and attention from their parents. In Islam stress has been laid on mercy and kindness to children. In Islam children have been given the rights of feeding, giving clothes and protection until they reach maturity. In the Quran, according to Surah Al-Baqarah, “and the one whose child it is, upon him is their food and clothing according to custom.” It is the right of children that they obtain love and affection from parents. Getting equal status is also their right. Above all monetary gifts …

Hazrat Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), deciding (a case) of a father and son, said that the son has these rights over the father: that he chooses a good mother for the child, gives him a good name and teaches him the Quran. It is the responsibility of parents and legal heirs that they deal with children with love and affection. The blessed Sunnah is full of incidents of love and affection. It is narrated from Hazrat Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that one day a Companion was going along with the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions). He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) walked towards the tent of Hazrat Fatimah (may Allah be pleased with her) and asked about the children. Suddenly Hazrat Hasan (may Allah be pleased with him) came running out and embraced him (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions). He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) began to say: “O Allah, I love him; You too love him, and love whoever loves him.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) kissed him in front of the Companion. The Companion said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have ten children and I have not kissed any one of them till today.” He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, his family and companions) said that whoever does not show mercy to others, mercy will not be shown to him.

Buying and selling:

In the world convention on children’s rights, states have been bound to control the buying and selling of children.

Identity:

According to Article 8, states shall ensure respect for the rights of children so that children can protect their identity, which includes their nationality, name and relation with the family etc., and unlawful interference in these rights is stopped. If the right to any part of identity has been taken from any child, states shall provide children help and protection in restoring their identity. Before Islam, in Arab society, the custom of adoption and taking as one’s own was common. The adopted child used the name of the adopting parents and the name of the family …
